# Helpdesk API

Rails API-only backend for a helpdesk SaaS. Businesses sign up, their owners verify
email and sign in, and each business has its own users. The frontend is a separate
app that talks to this API over JSON under `/api/v1`.

## Setup

Requires Ruby 4.0, PostgreSQL and the gems in the `Gemfile`.

```sh
bundle install
export DATABASE_URL=postgresql:///helpdesk_development?host=/var/lib/postgresql
bin/rails db:prepare                 # creates and migrates the development database
RAILS_ENV=test bin/rails db:prepare  # the test database (a "_test" sibling of DATABASE_URL)
bin/rails server                     # listens on PORT (default 3000)
bin/rails test                       # the suite never touches the development database
```

Outgoing mail is written to `tmp/mails/` in development.

### Environment variables

| Variable | Default | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `DATABASE_URL` | none (required) | PostgreSQL connection. |
| `TEST_DATABASE_URL` | `DATABASE_URL` with `_development` replaced by `_test` | Test database. Tests never use the development database. |
| `HELPDESK_FRONTEND_URL` | `http://localhost:3001` | Frontend base URL. Used for email links and as the only allowed CORS origin. |
| `HELPDESK_MAIL_FROM` | `support@example.test` | Sender address for all mail. |
| `SMTP_ADDRESS`, `SMTP_PORT`, `SMTP_DOMAIN`, `SMTP_USERNAME`, `SMTP_PASSWORD` | `localhost`, `587`, — | Production mail delivery. |

## Conventions

- Every request body uses an envelope, e.g. `{"session": {...}}`. Bare JSON is rejected.
- **Choosing a business:** send `X-Helpdesk-Account: <subdomain>`.
  - Signed-in requests can omit it. The token already identifies the business. If it is sent and does not match, the response is 403.
  - Sign-in, verification resend and password reset use it to find the user. Without it, the email must belong to exactly one business.
- **Signed-in requests:** send `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.
- **Lists** take `page` (default 1) and `per_page` (default 25, at most 100). They return the records under the plural resource name (`requests`, `tickets`, `comments`), plus `count` (all matches, not just this page), `page`, `per_page`, `next_page` and `previous_page`. The last two are `null` when there is no such page.
- **Errors** share one shape: `{"error": {"code": "...", "message": "...", "errors": {...}}}`. `errors` is present for validation failures. Validation keys are prefixed `account.` or `admin.` on signup.
- Timestamps are ISO 8601 UTC.

## Endpoints

| Method and path | Auth | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `POST /api/v1/registrations` | header required | Customer signs up for the business's portal, `{"user": {"name", "email", "password"}}`. Returns `201` with `user` (role `customer`). The user is unverified and gets a verification email. Then the usual verification, sign-in, profile and password-reset flows apply. |
| `POST /api/v1/account/create` | none | Sign up a business and its admin. Returns `201` with `account` and `user`. The admin is unverified and receives a verification email. |
| `GET /api/v1/portal` | header | Public `{"portal": {"name", "subdomain"}}`. |
| `POST /api/v1/sessions` | header optional | Sign in with `{"session": {"email", "password"}}`. Returns `201` with `session.token`, `user` and `account`. Unverified users get `403 email_not_verified`. |
| `DELETE /api/v1/session` | bearer | Sign out this session. `204`. |
| `GET /api/v1/me` / `PATCH /api/v1/me` | bearer | Profile. `PATCH` takes `{"user": {"name": "..."}}`. |
| `PUT /api/v1/me/password` | bearer | `{"password_change": {"current_password", "password"}}`. Signs out every session, including this one. |
| `POST /api/v1/email_verifications` | header optional | `{"email_verification": {"email"}}`. Sends a new link and replaces the old one. Returns `202`. |
| `POST /api/v1/email_verifications/confirm` | header optional | `{"email_verification": {"token"}}`. Marks the user verified. The token works once. |
| `POST /api/v1/password_resets` | header optional | `{"password_reset": {"email"}}`. Sends a new link and replaces the old one. Returns `202` whether or not the email exists. |
| `POST /api/v1/password_resets/confirm` | header optional | `{"password_reset": {"token", "password"}}`. Sets the password, signs out all sessions and verifies the email. The token works once. |
| `GET /api/v1/account` | bearer | Full account, including `status` and `reactivation_deadline`. |
| `POST /api/v1/account/cancel` | bearer, owner | Cancels the business and revokes all its sessions. |
| `POST /api/v1/account/reactivate` | bearer, owner | Reactivates a cancelled business within 90 days. |
| `GET /api/v1/requests` | bearer | The signed-in user's own requests, most recently active first, under `requests`. |
| `POST /api/v1/requests` | bearer | Open a request: `{"request": {"subject", "comment": {"body"}}}`. Returns `201` with `request`, which starts `open`. |
| `GET /api/v1/requests/:id` | bearer | One of your requests, under `request`. Another user's request returns `404`. |
| `PATCH /api/v1/requests/:id` | bearer | Reply: `{"request": {"comment": {"body"}, "status": "solved"}}`. Either key is optional, but send at least one. See [Requests](#requests). Returns `request`. |
| `GET /api/v1/requests/:id/comments` | bearer | Comments on your request, oldest first, under `comments`. |
| `GET /api/v1/tickets` | bearer, staff | Every request in the business, most recently active first, under `tickets`. Each one names its `requester` as `{"id", "name", "email"}`. |
| `GET /api/v1/tickets/:id` | bearer, staff | One request, under `ticket`. |
| `PATCH /api/v1/tickets/:id` | bearer, staff | Staff reply: `{"ticket": {"comment": {"body"}, "status": "pending"}}`. Returns `ticket`. See [Requests](#requests). |
| `GET /api/v1/tickets/:id/comments` | bearer, staff | Every comment on the request, oldest first, under `comments`. |

Emailed links:

- `HELPDESK_FRONTEND_URL/verify-email?account=<subdomain>&token=<token>`
- `HELPDESK_FRONTEND_URL/reset-password?account=<subdomain>&token=<token>`

Token lifetimes are 3 days for verification and 2 hours for password reset. Sessions last 30 days.

## Accounts and roles

- The signing-up user is an `admin` and acts as the business owner. Only admins can cancel or reactivate.
- An `agent` is staff, like an admin. The API does not create agents yet.
- A `customer` registers through the portal (`POST /registrations`). Customers can only reach their own requests. Staff-only routes return `403 staff_only` to them.
- Email addresses are unique within a business, so one email can belong to several businesses.
- Subdomains are unique across all businesses and must not be reserved (`www`, `api`, `app`, `admin`, ...).

### Cancellation

- `POST /account/cancel` sets `cancelled_at` and revokes every session in the business.
- While cancelled, only the owner can sign in. Ordinary access returns `403 account_cancelled`. The owner can still view the account, edit their profile, change their password, sign out, and reactivate.
- `POST /account/reactivate` works until 90 days after cancellation.
- Data is kept until the reactivation window closes.

### Permanent deletion

```sh
bin/rails helpdesk:purge_cancelled_accounts
```

This deletes every account cancelled more than 90 days ago, along with its users, sessions, tokens, requests and comments. Run it on a schedule, for example daily from cron. It is safe to run repeatedly.

## Requests

A request is one record with a subject, a status and a conversation. Customers see it at `/requests`, and staff at `/tickets`. Both views are the same records.

- A new request is `open`. Opening one needs a `subject` and a first `comment.body`. Both are saved, or neither is.
- Statuses are `open`, `pending` and `solved`.
- **Customer replies** can carry a comment, a status, or both. A status can only be `solved`, so `pending` or `open` is refused with `422`. A comment reopens a `pending` or `solved` request, unless the same update marks it `solved`.
- **Staff replies** can carry a comment, a status, or both. Any of the three statuses is allowed. A reply without a status leaves the status alone, so a staff reply never reopens a request by itself.
- A reply with a comment and a status is applied as one update. If either part is invalid, nothing is saved.
- Comments are always public for now. The API cannot post internal notes yet, so `public` is always `true`. Customers see only public comments on their own requests. Staff see every comment.
- Comment bodies are limited to 10,000 characters. Subjects are limited to 255.
- Replies send no email. The conversation is only in the portal.
- Activity moves a request up the lists: opening, replying, or changing its status. Comments are listed oldest first.

## Layout

- `app/models/account.rb`: business, cancellation, reactivation window, purge.
- `app/models/user.rb`: users, roles, password rules.
- `app/models/session.rb`: bearer sessions (only token digests are stored).
- `app/models/ticket.rb`: requests and their status rules. `app/models/comment.rb`: the conversation.
- `app/models/concerns/single_use_token.rb`: replaceable, single-use tokens for verification and reset.
- `app/controllers/concerns/`: error format, business lookup from header, bearer auth and cancelled-account rules, pagination, and reply parsing.
- `app/controllers/api/v1/`: endpoints.
- `app/mailers/user_mailer.rb`: verification and reset emails.
- `config/initializers/helpdesk.rb`: settings from the environment. `config/initializers/cors.rb`: frontend CORS.
"
}

class Account < ApplicationRecord
  # Cancelled accounts can be reactivated for this long, then purged for good.
  REACTIVATION_WINDOW = 90.days

  SUBDOMAIN_FORMAT = /\A[a-z0-9](?:[a-z0-9-]{0,61}[a-z0-9])\z/
  RESERVED_SUBDOMAINS = %w[admin api app assets mail smtp static status www].freeze

  # Declared before users, so requests and their comments go before the people who opened them.
  has_many :tickets, dependent: :destroy
  has_many :users, dependent: :destroy

  normalizes :name, with: ->(value) { value.to_s.strip }
  normalizes :subdomain, with: ->(value) { value.to_s.strip.downcase }

  validates :name, presence: true, length: { maximum: 120 }
  validates :subdomain,
            presence: true,
            uniqueness: true,
            format: { with: SUBDOMAIN_FORMAT, message: "may only use lowercase letters, digits and hyphens" },
            exclusion: { in: RESERVED_SUBDOMAINS, message: "is reserved" }

  scope :cancelled_before, ->(time) { where(cancelled_at: ..time) }

  def cancelled?
    cancelled_at.present?
  end

  def reactivation_deadline
    cancelled_at && (cancelled_at + REACTIVATION_WINDOW)
  end

  def reactivation_open?(now = Time.current)
    cancelled? && now < reactivation_deadline
  end

  # Cancelling stops ordinary access and signs every user out. The data is kept
  # until the reactivation window closes.
  def cancel!(now: Time.current)
    transaction do
      update!(cancelled_at: now)
      Session.where(user_id: users.select(:id)).delete_all
    end
  end

  def reactivate!
    update!(cancelled_at: nil)
  end

  # Permanently deletes accounts cancelled more than REACTIVATION_WINDOW ago,
  # along with all their users, sessions, tokens, requests and comments. Returns the number purged.
  def self.purge_cancelled!(now: Time.current)
    cutoff = now - REACTIVATION_WINDOW
    purged = 0

    cancelled_before(cutoff).ids.each do |id|
      transaction do
        # Re-check under a row lock: the account may have been reactivated since the query.
        account = lock.find_by(id: id)
        next unless account&.cancelled_at && account.cancelled_at <= cutoff

        account.destroy!
        purged += 1
      end
    end

    purged
  end

  def as_api_json
    {
      id: id,
      name: name,
      subdomain: subdomain,
      status: cancelled? ? "cancelled" : "active",
      cancelled_at: cancelled_at,
      reactivation_deadline: reactivation_deadline,
      created_at: created_at,
      updated_at: updated_at
    }
  end
end

class Session < ApplicationRecord
  TTL = 30.days

  belongs_to :user

  validates :token_digest, :expires_at, presence: true

  # Returns [session, raw_token]. The raw token is shown once, at sign-in.
  def self.issue!(user)
    raw = SecureRandom.urlsafe_base64(32)
    session = user.sessions.create!(token_digest: digest(raw), expires_at: TTL.from_now)

class Ticket < ApplicationRecord
  STATUSES = %w[open pending solved].freeze
  # Customers can only mark a request solved. Staff can choose any status.
  CUSTOMER_STATUSES = %w[solved].freeze

  belongs_to :account
  belongs_to :requester, class_name: "User"
  has_many :comments, -> { order(:created_at, :id) }, dependent: :delete_all, inverse_of: :ticket

  normalizes :subject, with: ->(value) { value.to_s.strip }

  validates :subject, presence: true, length: { maximum: 255 }
  validates :status, inclusion: { in: STATUSES }
  validate :requester_belongs_to_account

  # Most recently active first. The id breaks ties so pages never repeat or skip records.
  scope :recently_active, -> { order(updated_at: :desc, id: :desc) }
  scope :requested_by, ->(user) { where(requester: user) }

  # Opens a request from +requester+ with its first comment. Both are saved, or neither is.
  def self.open!(requester:, subject:, body:)
    ticket = new(account: requester.account, requester: requester, subject: subject, status: "open")
    ticket.reply!(author: requester, body: body, customer: true)
  end

  # Posts a reply and/or changes the status, in one transaction.
  #
  # body:     the comment to post. nil posts nothing. Blank is an error.
  # status:   the status to set. nil keeps the current one.
  # customer: customers may only mark the request solved. A customer reply reopens
  #           a pending or solved request, unless it is solved in the same update.
  #           A staff reply never changes the status by itself.
  def reply!(author:, body: nil, status: nil, customer: false)
    update_with_comment!(author: author, body: body, status: status, customer: customer)
  end

  # What customers see: their own request, without the requester's details.
  def as_request_json
    {
      id: id,
      subject: subject,
      status: status,
      requester_id: requester_id,
      created_at: created_at,
      updated_at: updated_at
    }
  end

  # What staff see, including who opened the request.
  def as_ticket_json
    {
      id: id,
      subject: subject,
      status: status,
      requester: { id: requester.id, name: requester.name, email: requester.email },
      created_at: created_at,
      updated_at: updated_at
    }
  end

  private

  def update_with_comment!(author:, body: nil, status: nil, customer: false)
    comment = Comment.new(ticket: self, author: author, body: body) unless body.nil?
    self.status = next_status(requested: status, replying: !comment.nil?, customer: customer)

    # valid? clears earlier errors, so the checks below must come after it.
    valid?
    if customer && STATUSES.include?(status) && CUSTOMER_STATUSES.exclude?(status)
      errors.add(:status, "customers can only mark a request solved")
    end
    copy_comment_errors(comment)
    raise ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid, self if errors.any?

    transaction do
      save!
      comment&.save!
    end
    self
  end

  def next_status(requested:, replying:, customer:)
    return requested unless requested.nil?
    # A customer's reply reopens. An open request stays open.
    return "open" if customer && replying

    status
  end

  # Errors from the comment are reported as "comment.<field>", next to the ticket's own.
  def copy_comment_errors(comment)
    return if comment.nil? || comment.valid?

    comment.errors.each { |error| errors.add(:"comment.#{error.attribute}", error.message) }
  end

  def requester_belongs_to_account
    return if requester.nil? || requester.account_id == account_id

    errors.add(:requester, "must belong to the same business")
  end
end

# Emailed tokens (email verification, password reset). Each user has at most one
# live token of each kind. Issuing a new one replaces the old, and redeeming a
# token deletes it, so it works once.
module SingleUseToken
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  # Raised when a token is unknown, expired, already used, or for another business.
  class InvalidToken < StandardError; end

  included do
    belongs_to :user

    validates :token_digest, :expires_at, presence: true
  end

  class_methods do
    # Returns the raw token to email. Only its digest is stored.
    def issue!(user)
      raw = SecureRandom.urlsafe_base64(32)
      user.with_lock do
        where(user_id: user.id).delete_all
        create!(user: user, token_digest: digest(raw), expires_at: self::TTL.from_now)
      end
      raw
    end

    # Deletes and returns the matching token record, or raises InvalidToken.
    # Call inside a transaction, so a later failure also gives the token back.
    def redeem!(raw, account: nil)
      scope = where(token_digest: digest(raw))
      scope = scope.where(user_id: account.users.select(:id)) if account

      record = scope.lock.first
      raise InvalidToken unless record&.expires_at&.future?

      record.destroy!
      record
    end

    def digest(raw)
      Digest::SHA256.hexdigest(raw.to_s)
    end
  end
end
class EmailVerification < ApplicationRecord
  include SingleUseToken

  TTL = 3.days
end
class PasswordReset < ApplicationRecord
  include SingleUseToken

  TTL = 2.hours
end
class ApplicationRecord < ActiveRecord::Base
  primary_abstract_class
end

module AccountScoped
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

# Bearer-token sessions. Callers include `before_action :authenticate_session!`.
#
# A cancelled account blocks everything except the actions listed with
# `available_while_cancelled`, which the owner needs to reactivate the account.
module Authenticatable
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  included do
    class_attribute :cancelled_account_actions, instance_writer: false, default: [].freeze
  end

  class_methods do
    def available_while_cancelled(*actions)
      self.cancelled_account_actions = (cancelled_account_actions + actions.map(&:to_s)).freeze
    end
  end

  private

  attr_reader :current_session, :current_user, :current_account

  def authenticate_session!
    session = Session.find_active(bearer_token)
    return render_error(:unauthorized, "unauthenticated", "Sign in to continue.") unless session

    user = session.user
    account = user.account

    if requested_subdomain && requested_subdomain != account.subdomain
      return render_error(:forbidden, "account_mismatch", "This session belongs to a different business.")
    end

    @current_session = session
    @current_user = user
    @current_account = account

    return if !account.cancelled? || self.class.cancelled_account_actions.include?(action_name)

    render_error(:forbidden, "account_cancelled", "This business has been cancelled.")
  end

  def require_account_owner!
    return if current_user.admin?

    render_error(:forbidden, "owner_only", "Only the account owner can do that.")
  end

  # Staff (admins and agents) work the helpdesk. Customers only see their own requests.
  def require_staff!
    return if current_user.staff?

    render_error(:forbidden, "staff_only", "Only business staff can do that.")
  end

  def bearer_token
    request.authorization.to_s[/\ABearer\s+(\S+)\z/i, 1]
  end
end
# Every error response has the same shape:
#   {"error": {"code": "...", "message": "...", "errors": {...}}}
# where "errors" is present only for validation failures.
module ErrorHandling
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  included do
    rescue_from ActionController::ParameterMissing, with: :render_parameter_missing
    rescue_from ActionDispatch::Http::Parameters::ParseError, with: :render_bad_json
    rescue_from ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid, with: :render_record_invalid
    rescue_from ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique, with: :render_record_not_unique
    rescue_from ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound, with: :render_record_not_found
    rescue_from SingleUseToken::InvalidToken, with: :render_invalid_token
  end

  private

  # Like params.require, but a value that is not an object (e.g. a bare string)
  # counts as missing, so the client gets a 400 instead of a server error.
  def require_params(key)
    value = params.require(key)
    raise ActionController::ParameterMissing, key unless value.is_a?(ActionController::Parameters)

    value
  end

  def render_error(status, code, message, errors: nil)
    body = { code: code, message: message }
    body[:errors] = errors if errors.present?
    render json: { error: body }, status: status
  end

  def render_validation_failed(errors)
    render_error(:unprocessable_entity, "validation_failed", "Some fields are invalid.", errors: errors)
  end

  def render_parameter_missing(exception)
    render_error(:bad_request, "parameter_missing", exception.message)
  end

  def render_bad_json(_exception)
    render_error(:bad_request, "invalid_json", "The request body is not valid JSON.")
  end

  def render_record_invalid(exception)
    render_validation_failed(exception.record.errors.to_hash)
  end

  def render_record_not_unique(_exception)
    render_error(:conflict, "conflict", "That record was created by another request. Please try again.")
  end

  def render_record_not_found(_exception)
    render_error(:not_found, "not_found", "The requested record was not found.")
  end

  def render_invalid_token(_exception)
    render_error(:unprocessable_entity, "invalid_token", "This link is invalid or has expired. Request a new one.")
  end
end
# Offset pagination for list endpoints, using ?page= and ?per_page= (defaults 1 and 25).
#
# The response holds the records under +key+, plus count (all matches, not just
# this page), page, per_page, next_page and previous_page. The last two are null
# when there is no such page.
module Paginated
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  DEFAULT_PER_PAGE = 25
  MAX_PER_PAGE = 100

  private

  def render_page(scope, key:, &serialize)
    errors = {}
    page = whole_number_param(:page, 1, errors)
    per_page = whole_number_param(:per_page, DEFAULT_PER_PAGE, errors, max: MAX_PER_PAGE)
    return render_validation_failed(errors) if errors.any?

    count = scope.count
    offset = (page - 1) * per_page
    # Past the end there is nothing to fetch. Skipping the query also keeps huge page numbers away from SQL.
    records = offset < count ? scope.offset(offset).limit(per_page).to_a : []

    render json: {
      key => records.map(&serialize),
      count: count,
      page: page,
      per_page: per_page,
      next_page: page * per_page < count ? page + 1 : nil,
      previous_page: page > 1 ? page - 1 : nil
    }
  end

  # Reads a positive whole number from the query string. Anything else adds an
  # error for +name+ and returns nil.
  def whole_number_param(name, default, errors, max: nil)
    raw = params[name].to_s.strip
    return default if raw.empty?

    number = raw.to_i if raw.match?(/\A\d+\z/)
    return number if number&.positive? && (max.nil? || number <= max)

    errors[name] = [ max ? "must be a whole number from 1 to #{max}" : "must be a whole number of at least 1" ]
    nil
  end
end
# Reads a reply from a PATCH body. A reply can carry a comment, a status, or both.
module Replies
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  private

  # The comment body to post. nil when the reply has no comment.
  def reply_body(input)
    input.key?(:comment) ? input.dig(:comment, :body).to_s : nil
  end

  # The status to set. nil leaves the status alone.
  def reply_status(input)
    input.key?(:status) ? input[:status].to_s : nil
  end

  # Renders 400 and returns true when the reply has neither a comment nor a status.
  def reject_empty_reply(input)
    return false if input.key?(:comment) || input.key?(:status)

    render_error(:bad_request, "parameter_missing", "Send a comment, a status, or both.")
    true
  end
end

    DEFAULT_FRONTEND_URL = "http://localhost:3001".freeze

    request_headers = { "Accept" => "application/json" }.merge(headers)
    request_headers["Authorization"] = "Bearer #{token}" if token

  # Token from the newest mail sent to `to` whose link is for `account` and `path`.
  # Links carry the business, so two businesses sharing an email stay distinct.
  def link_token(to:, path:, account:)
    mail = ActionMailer::Base.deliveries.reverse.find do |candidate|
      Array(candidate.to).include?(to) && candidate.body.decoded.include?("#{path}?account=#{account}&")
    end
    assert mail, "expected an email to #{to} linking to #{path} for #{account}"

    link = mail.body.decoded[%r{http://\S+}]
    Rack::Utils.parse_query(URI.parse(link).query).fetch("token")
  end

  def verification_token(email, account: "acme")
    link_token(to: email, path: "/verify-email", account: account)

steps.message:
`save!(touch: false)` is supported, so an assignment can avoid bumping `updated_at`. I now have enough context to design this.

My plan, based on the codebase's existing conventions:

- **Invitations**: a new table with a token digest, timestamps for `accepted_at`/`revoked_at`, and an `expires_at`. Status is derived from those, and the list supports a `status` filter. Issuing, resending, revoking, accepting, customer registration and suspension all run under the account row lock (the same pattern as `EmailVerification.issue!`). That keeps the "no competing invitations" and "last active admin" rules race-free.
- **Suspension**: a `suspended` boolean on users. Suspending deletes their sessions and nulls `tickets.assignee_id` without touching `updated_at`.
- **Assignment**: `assignee_id` on tickets. Assignment and private notes must not move the request, so `Comment` stops touching the ticket on every save. Only public comments and status changes do.
- **Private notes**: a strict `comment.public` flag on the staff endpoint. Anything other than a boolean is refused, so a typo can't post a note publicly.

Before writing any code, I'll write the tests that describe this behaviour and confirm they fail. I'll start with shared helpers.

arguments.command:
cd /app && cat > app/models/invitation.rb <<'EOF'
# An emailed offer to join a business as an admin or agent. Customers register on their own, so they are never invited.
#
# Status comes from the timestamps, so expiry needs no job:
#   accepted  accepted_at is set
#   revoked   revoked_at is set, by an admin
#   pending   neither is set, and expires_at is in the future
#   expired   neither is set, and expires_at has passed
#
# An email can hold at most one pending invitation in a business, and cannot be invited when it already belongs
# to a user there. Issuing, resending, revoking and accepting all run under the account's row lock, as do customer
# registration and suspension, so two requests cannot both pass these checks.
class Invitation < ApplicationRecord
  TTL = 7.days
  ROLES = %w[admin agent].freeze
  STATUSES = %w[pending accepted revoked expired].freeze

  # Raised when a token is unknown, expired, revoked, accepted, or for another business.
  class InvalidInvitation < StandardError; end
  # Raised when an admin resends or revokes an invitation that was already accepted or revoked.
  class AlreadyClosed < StandardError; end

  belongs_to :account
  belongs_to :invited_by, class_name: "User", optional: true

  normalizes :email, with: ->(value) { value.to_s.strip.downcase }

  validates :email, presence: true, length: { maximum: 254 }, format: { with: URI::MailTo::EMAIL_REGEXP }
  validates :role, inclusion: { in: ROLES, message: "must be admin or agent" }
  validates :token_digest, :expires_at, presence: true
  # Only checked when an invitation is issued or resent, so existing records do not start failing later.
  validate :email_must_be_free, on: :issue

  # Invitations in one status. Accepted and revoked are final. Pending and expired depend on the clock.
  def self.with_status(status)
    now = Time.current
    open = where(accepted_at: nil, revoked_at: nil)

    case status
    when "pending" then open.where("expires_at > ?", now)
    when "expired" then open.where("expires_at <= ?", now)
    when "accepted" then where.not(accepted_at: nil)
    when "revoked" then where(accepted_at: nil).where.not(revoked_at: nil)
    else raise ArgumentError, "unknown invitation status #{status.inspect}"
    end
  end

  # Returns [invitation, raw_token]. The raw token is only emailed, never stored or shown in the API.
  def self.issue!(account:, invited_by:, email:, role:)
    raw = generate_token
    invitation = nil
    account.with_lock do
      invitation = new(account: account, invited_by: invited_by, email: email, role: role,
                       token_digest: digest(raw), expires_at: TTL.from_now)
      invitation.save!(context: :issue)
    end
    [ invitation, raw ]
  end

  # The pending invitation that +raw+ opens. Raises InvalidInvitation for anything else. When +account+ is given,
  # the invitation must belong to it.
  def self.find_pending_by_token!(raw, account: nil, now: Time.current)
    raise InvalidInvitation if raw.blank?

    scope = where(token_digest: digest(raw))
    scope = scope.where(account: account) if account
    invitation = scope.includes(:account).first
    raise InvalidInvitation unless invitation&.status(now) == "pending"

    invitation
  end

  def self.digest(raw)
    Digest::SHA256.hexdigest(raw.to_s)
  end

  def self.generate_token
    SecureRandom.urlsafe_base64(32)
  end

  def status(now = Time.current)
    return "accepted" if accepted_at
    return "revoked" if revoked_at

    expires_at > now ? "pending" : "expired"
  end

  def open?
    accepted_at.nil? && revoked_at.nil?
  end

  # Replaces the token and restarts the clock. The old link stops working. Works for pending and expired
  # invitations. Returns the new raw token.
  def resend!
    raw = self.class.generate_token
    account.with_lock do
      reload
      raise AlreadyClosed unless open?

      self.token_digest = self.class.digest(raw)
      self.expires_at = TTL.from_now
      save!(context: :issue)
    end
    raw
  end

  # Cancels a pending or expired invitation. The record stays, marked revoked.
  def revoke!(now: Time.current)
    account.with_lock do
      reload
      raise AlreadyClosed unless open?

      update!(revoked_at: now)
    end
  end

  # Creates the verified user with the invited email and role, and marks the invitation accepted. Both happen, or neither does.
  def accept!(name:, password:, now: Time.current)
    account.with_lock do
      reload
      raise InvalidInvitation unless status(now) == "pending"

      user = account.users.create!(name: name, email: email, password: password, role: role, verified_at: now)
      update!(accepted_at: now)
      user
    end
  end

  def as_api_json(now: Time.current)
    {
      id: id,
      email: email,
      role: role,
      status: status(now),

# A customer's request for help and the conversation about it. Customers see it
# as a "request", staff as a "ticket". It is one record.
class Ticket < ApplicationRecord
  STATUSES = %w[open pending solved].freeze
  # Customers can only mark a request solved. Staff can choose any status.
  CUSTOMER_STATUSES = %w[solved].freeze
  # Default for an argument that was not sent. Unlike nil, which means "clear it" for the assignee.
  UNCHANGED = Object.new.freeze

  belongs_to :account
  belongs_to :requester, class_name: "User"
  belongs_to :assignee, class_name: "User", optional: true
  has_many :comments, -> { order(:created_at, :id) }, dependent: :delete_all, inverse_of: :ticket

  normalizes :subject, with: ->(value) { value.to_s.strip }

  validates :subject, presence: true, length: { maximum: 255 }
  validates :status, inclusion: { in: STATUSES }
  validate :requester_belongs_to_account
  validate :assignee_must_be_active_staff, if: :will_save_change_to_assignee_id?

  # Most recently active first. The id breaks ties so pages never repeat or skip records.
  scope :recently_active, -> { order(updated_at: :desc, id: :desc) }
  scope :requested_by, ->(user) { where(requester: user) }

  # Opens a request from +requester+ with its first comment. Both are saved, or neither is.
  def self.open!(requester:, subject:, body:)
    ticket = new(account: requester.account, requester: requester, subject: subject, status: "open")
    ticket.reply!(author: requester, body: body, customer: true)
  end

  # Posts a reply, changes the status and/or changes the assignee, in one transaction.
  #
  # body:           the comment to post. nil posts nothing. Blank is an error.
  # status:         the status to set. nil keeps the current one.
  # customer:       customers may only mark the request solved. A customer reply reopens
  #                 a pending or solved request, unless it is solved in the same update.
  #                 A staff reply never changes the status by itself.
  # public_comment: false posts a private note, which only staff can see. Customers always post public comments.
  # assignee_id:    the staff member to assign, nil to clear, or UNCHANGED to leave it alone.
  #
  # Only a status change or a public comment counts as activity and moves the request up the lists. Assigning
  # and private notes leave the request's timestamps alone.
  def reply!(author:, body: nil, status: nil, customer: false, public_comment: true, assignee_id: UNCHANGED)
    update_with_comment!(author: author, body: body, status: status, customer: customer,
                         public_comment: public_comment, assignee_id: assignee_id)
  end

  # What customers see: their own request, without the requester's details.
  def as_request_json
    {
      id: id,
      subject: subject,
      status: status,
      requester_id: requester_id,
      created_at: created_at,
      updated_at: updated_at
    }
  end

  # What staff see, including who opened the request and who is working on it.
  def as_ticket_json
    {
      id: id,
      subject: subject,
      status: status,
      requester: { id: requester.id, name: requester.name, email: requester.email },
      assignee_id: assignee_id,
      assignee: assignee && { id: assignee.id, name: assignee.name },
      created_at: created_at,
      updated_at: updated_at
    }
  end

  private

  def update_with_comment!(author:, body:, status:, customer:, public_comment:, assignee_id:)
    comment = Comment.new(ticket: self, author: author, body: body, public: customer || public_comment) unless body.nil?
    self.status = next_status(requested: status, replying: !comment.nil?, customer: customer)
    self.assignee_id = assignee_id unless assignee_id.equal?(UNCHANGED)

    # valid? clears earlier errors, so the checks below must come after it.
    valid?
    if customer && STATUSES.include?(status) && CUSTOMER_STATUSES.exclude?(status)
      errors.add(:status, "customers can only mark a request solved")
    end
    copy_comment_errors(comment)
    raise ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid, self if errors.any?

    transaction do
      # Only a status change bumps the request's timestamp here. Assigning does not, and a public comment bumps it when saved.
      save!(touch: !will_save_change_to_status?)
      comment&.save!
    end
    self
  end

  def next_status(requested:, replying:, customer:)
    return requested unless requested.nil?
    # A customer's reply reopens. An open request stays open.
    return "open" if customer && replying

    status
  end

  # Errors from the comment are reported as "comment.<field>", next to the ticket's own.
  def copy_comment_errors(comment)
    return if comment.nil? || comment.valid?

    comment.errors.each { |error| errors.add(:"comment.#{error.attribute}", error.message) }
  end

  def requester_belongs_to_account
    return if requester.nil? || requester.account_id == account_id

    errors.add(:requester, "must belong to the same business")
  end

  # Only active staff in the same business can work a request.
  def assignee_must_be_active_staff
    return if assignee_id.nil?
    return if assignee && assignee.account_id == account_id && assignee.staff? && !assignee.suspended?

    errors.add(:assignee_id, "must be an active staff member of this business")
  end
end

# Reads a reply from a PATCH body. A reply can carry a comment, a status, or both.
module Replies
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  private

  # The comment body to post. nil when the reply has no comment.
  def reply_body(input)
    input.key?(:comment) ? input.dig(:comment, :body).to_s : nil
  end

  # The status to set. nil leaves the status alone.
  def reply_status(input)
    input.key?(:status) ? input[:status].to_s : nil
  end

  # Renders 400 and returns true when the update names none of +keys+. The default keys are a comment and a status.
  def reject_empty_reply(input, keys: %i[comment status], message: "Send a comment, a status, or both.")

  "output": "# An emailed offer to join a business as an admin or agent. Customers register on their own, so they are never invited.

#   expired   neither is set, and expires_at has passed
#
# An email can hold at most one pending invitation in a business, and cannot be invited when it already belongs
# to a user there. Issuing, resending, revoking and accepting all run under the account's row lock, as do customer
# registration and suspension, so two requests cannot both pass these checks.
class Invitation < ApplicationRecord
  TTL = 7.days
  ROLES = %w[admin agent].freeze
  STATUSES = %w[pending accepted revoked expired].freeze

  # Raised when a token is unknown, expired, revoked, accepted, or for another business.
  class InvalidInvitation < StandardError; end
  # Raised when an admin resends or revokes an invitation that was already accepted or revoked.
  class AlreadyClosed < StandardError; end

  belongs_to :account
  belongs_to :invited_by, class_name: "User", optional: true

  normalizes :email, with: ->(value) { value.to_s.strip.downcase }

  validates :email, presence: true, length: { maximum: 254 }, format: { with: URI::MailTo::EMAIL_REGEXP }
  validates :role, inclusion: { in: ROLES, message: "must be admin or agent" }
  validates :token_digest, :expires_at, presence: true
  # Only checked when an invitation is issued or resent, so existing records do not start failing later.
  validate :email_must_be_free, on: :issue

  # Invitations in one status. Accepted and revoked are final. Pending and expired depend on the clock.
  def self.with_status(status)
    now = Time.current
    unanswered = where(accepted_at: nil, revoked_at: nil)

    case status
    when "pending" then unanswered.where("expires_at > ?", now)
    when "expired" then unanswered.where("expires_at <= ?", now)
    when "accepted" then where.not(accepted_at: nil)
    when "revoked" then where(accepted_at: nil).where.not(revoked_at: nil)
    else raise ArgumentError, "unknown invitation status #{status.inspect}"
    end
  end

  # Returns [invitation, raw_token]. The raw token is only emailed, never stored or shown in the API.
  def self.issue!(account:, invited_by:, email:, role:)
    raw = generate_token
    invitation = nil
    account.with_lock do
      invitation = new(account: account, invited_by: invited_by, email: email, role: role,
                       token_digest: digest(raw), expires_at: TTL.from_now)
      invitation.save!(context: :issue)
    end
    [ invitation, raw ]
  end

  # the invitation must belong to it.

steps.message:
Everything is in place. The full suite passed on the final code (219 runs, 0 failures), and the README matches the behaviour. I'll submit now.

**Summary of what was built**

Invitations, user management, suspension, staff choices, ticket assignment and private notes are all in `/app`. The suite now has 219 tests, all passing. That's the original 117 plus 102 new ones. I also ran a real-HTTP smoke test on the development server, then removed its data.

- **Invitations** (`POST/GET/GET :id/POST resend/DELETE` under `/api/v1/invitations`): admins only. Tokens are emailed as `/accept-invitation?account=…&token=…` and only their digest is stored. Status (pending, accepted, revoked, expired) is derived from timestamps, and `?status=` filters the list. The API never returns a token.
- **Preview and acceptance** (`/invitation_previews`, `/invitation_acceptances`): acceptance creates a verified user, so Sam can sign in with no second email.
- **No competing invitations**: one pending invitation per email per business, and no invite for an email that already belongs to a user there. Customer registration refuses a pending invitation's email, reporting it as "taken" so the portal doesn't reveal who was invited.
- **Users** (`GET /users`, `GET /users/:id`, `PATCH /users/:id`): filters for role and suspension. Suspension signs the person out, clears their assignments without touching timestamps, and blocks sign-in. The last active admin cannot be suspended.
- **`GET /staff`**: active (not suspended) admins and agents, by ID.
- **Tickets**: `assignee_id` (or `null`) on staff updates, with `assignee: {id, name}` in the staff JSON. Assignees must be active staff in the same business.
- **Private notes**: `comment.public: false` on the staff endpoint. A private note or an assignment leaves the customer's request byte-identical, which the smoke test confirmed.

**Concurrency**: issuing, resending, revoking and accepting invitations, registration, suspension, and assignee changes all run under the business row lock. Three concurrent checks each produced exactly one winner, and the last admin survived. The third check simulated the registration path rather than calling the controller.

**Decisions the spec didn't settle**
- Invitations last 7 days. Invite and resend return 201 and 200. Revoke returns 200 with the invitation, not 204.
- Accepted or revoked invitations can't be resent or revoked (`invitation_closed`). Pending or expired ones can. Revoking an expired one shows it as revoked.
- "Active" staff means not suspended. It doesn't require email verification, so an unverified signup owner appears in `/staff`.
- `public` and `suspended` accept only true/false (or those strings). Anything else returns 422. This prevents a typo from posting a note publicly.
- `PATCH /users/:id` changes only `suspended`. Other fields are ignored, as on `/me`.

**Changes to existing behaviour**
- Two existing tests were updated because the spec changes them. The ticket key list now includes the assignee fields. The "comments are always public" test now checks private notes.
- `Comment` no longer touches its ticket on every save. Only public comments do, so any code that creates private comments directly no longer bumps the request.
- Three migrations were added, and `db/schema.rb` was regenerated. Run `db:migrate` in every environment.

**Noticed, not changed**: the `users.role` column defaults to `agent`, which makes any user created without an explicit role staff. Current signup and registration always set the role, so nothing is exposed today, but the default is worth changing to `customer`.
